Cimarron County started the month out in exceptional drought (D4) in the central to western portions, while the east and far southern portions were in extreme drought (D3). A very small portion in the very far southeast was in severe drought (D2). Cimarron County was able to tap into some good monsoonal moisture during the month with much of the county receiving 3 to 5 of rain over the course of the month. This allowed the majority of the county to improve to severe drought (D2) while the far northwestern to north-central portion of the county remained in extreme drought.

Texas County started the month out with Extreme Drought (D3) conditions in the northwestern portion of the county with Severe Drought (D2) conditions elsewhere. With increased monsoonal moisture over portions of the Desert Southwest and some of that moisture creeping into the western combined Panhandles, the western portions of the county improved in drought while the east saw degradation. The far western portion of Texas County ended the month around 0.5 above normal while the central portions of the county ended the month around 0.5 below normal. The far eastern portion of the county had ended the month closer to 1 below normal.

Beaver County started the month of July with Extreme Drought (D3) across the northern third of the county and Severe Drought (D2) across the remainder of the county except for the far southeast where the drought conditions were in Moderate Drought (D1). Through the month, not much changed in the drought conditions with minor and limited rainfall amounts. Towards the middle of the month, a dry spell led to worsening of drought conditions with much of the county switching to Extreme Drought and Severe Drought persisting in the southeast by July 26. Beaver County received about 2 to 6 during the month of July and a majority of that fell over July 29-31, which brought drought conditions back to where they were at start the month.

Dallam County began the month of July with Exceptional Drought (D4) conditions across the far west, with Extreme Drought (D3) across the western half, and portions of the far north and northeast. The central and southeast portions of the county were in Severe Drought (D2) to start off the month. Overall, Dallam County received about 3 to 6 for a majority of the county during the month of July. The small area of Exceptional Drought conditions improved to Extreme Drought due to 1.5 to 2.5 across a majority of the county on July 12. The Extreme Drought only existed across the western portions of the county by mid month while the remainder of the county remained in Severe Drought. The remainder of the rainfall for the month generally fell during the July 29-31 rainfall event, which put almost all of Dallam County in Severe Drought, except for a small sliver in the west remaining Extreme Drought.

Sherman County was in Extreme Drought (D3) across the west and south central portion of the county at the beginning of July and Severe Drought (D2) for the remainder of the area. Much of the western portions of the county received 3 to 6 with even a small area of up to 8 of rainfall. A good third of the rainfall in the west fell during the first half of the month with drought conditions improving to Severe Drought across the entire county. A dry spell occurred for the second half of the month with the areas across the eastern half of the county declining to Extreme Drought until the 3 day rainfall event at the end of the month, which left the entire county back in Severe Drought to end July.

Hansford County began the month of July in Severe Drought (D2) across the northwest two-thirds of the county, while the southeast one-third was in Moderate Drought (D1). Small amounts of rainfall fell across the county leaving conditions the same until mid-month when conditions worsened to severe drought across the entire county. Most of the rainfall for Hansford County fell at the end of the month, therefore drought conditions continued to degraded to Extreme Drought (D3) across a majority of the county by the last week in July. However, about 1 to 2 fell across the county over July 29-31 and the drought conditions improved to severe drought to end the month.

Most of Lipscomb County started the month of July in Moderate Drought (D1) conditions, except for the northwest portion that was in Severe Drought (D2). Despite receiving 2 to 4 across most of the county and an area of 4 to 6 across the northwest through the month of July, the drought condition worsened by mid-month to Severe Drought across the entire county and remained at this state through the end of the month.

The far western sliver of Hartley County began the month of July in Exceptional Drought (D4), while the remainder of the western two-thirds of the county is in Extreme Drought (D3) and eastern third of the county is in Severe Drought (D2). The first half of the month the county received minimal precipitation with worsening drought conditions and an expansion of the exceptional drought eastward filling in the western third of the county. The remainder of the drought conditions across the county did not change from the beginning of the month. July 12th Hartley County received 1 to 3 of rainfall across the west and northwest, which led to complete improvement of the exceptional drought. Another event at the end of the month led to several days of rainfall and a total of 2 to 4 across the county, helping to lead to over 150% and above of normal value. This final event led to Hartley County ending the month in overall improvement to Severe Drought across the entire county.

Moore County begins the month with three separate drought classifications. Extreme Drought (D3) across the north central, Severe Drought (D2) portions of the north and east, and Moderate Drought (D1) to fill in the remainder of the county. Extreme Drought conditions were improved during the first two weeks of July with just a small amount of rainfall, less than an inch over the first two weeks. Total rainfall across Moore County for the month was about 2 to 5, with a majority of this falling at the end of the month across the south and southwest. Drought conditions across the county ended the month of July where a small sliver of Extreme Drought improved across the far southwest. The entire Moore County ended the month in Severe Drought.

Hutchinson County started the month of July with mostly Moderate Drought (D1) and a small area of Abnormally Dry (D0) across the southeast. The county received generally less than 3 of rainfall for the month, which is around or slightly below normal. Therefore the drought conditions by mid-month degraded across much of the county to Severe Drought. By the end of the month, the entire county was under Severe Drought conditions.

Hemphill County started the month in mostly Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions. For most of the county, the rainfall was below normal with drought conditions worsening to Moderate Drought (D1) and a sliver of Severe Drought (D2) across the far north central portion of the county. In the last few days of the month, conditions improved across the east to Abnormally Dry due to 2 to 3 of rainfall.

Drought conditions in Oldham County were mostly Extreme Drought (D3) with a sliver in the west of Exceptional Drought (D4) at the beginning of July. With minimal precipitation of 1 to 2 across portions of the county up until the last week of July, these conditions led to the drought conditions worsening and the western half of the county in Exceptional Drought and the remainder in Extreme Drought. On July 12, a wildfire broke out in the county due to breezy winds, low relative humidity, and highly receptive and dry fuels. However, in the last few days of July the county received a majority of its rainfall for the month. With about 4 to 8 across the area, the drought was significantly improved by the end of July with only the western half of the county in Extreme Drought and the eastern half in Severe Drought (D2).

Potter County at the beginning of July was in Extreme Drought across the western half of the county and then Severe Drought (D2) leading into Moderate Drought (D1) moving eastward. Minimal rainfall in the first three weeks of July lead to an increase in the Extreme Drought conditions across much of the southwest two-thirds of the county with Severe Drought in the rest. On July 3, a wildfire occurred due to strong winds, low relative humidity, and receptive fuels. A couple days of rainfall at the end of July lead to drought conditions improving across Potter County. In total about 3 to 6 of rainfall fell with the drought improving to mostly Severe Drought across the county.

Carson County started the month of July with the northeastern third to half in abnormally dry (D0) conditions. The southwest was in Moderate Drought (D1) with a very small portion in the southwest corner of the county in Severe Drought (D2). July was an abnormally hot and dry month with the area of D2 degrading to Extreme Drought and the area of D1 and D0 quickly reaching Severe Drought (D2) by the end of the second and third week. It wasn't until the very last 2 to 3 days of the month where the majority of the monthly rain fell and conditions improved to D1 for the majority of the county with the far northwest and southwest corners remaining in D2.

The north-central to eastern two thirds of the county started the month in Extreme Drought (D3) with the remaining western to southwestern portion in Exceptional Drought (D4). July was an abnormally warm and dry month especially up until the last few days. By mid month the majority of the county was in D4, with the exception of a small portion in the northeast corner that stayed in D3. The southern half of the county received 1.5 to 3.5 by the end of the month mostly thanks to a rain event over the last few days of the month. During these last few days the rest of the county ended the month with a grand total of 3.5 to 7 of rain. This allowed some improvement mainly in the north and east becoming D3 and D2 once again, while the majority of the southern to western half stayed in D4.

Randall County started the month with the west to northwest third of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). By mid month the entire county was in Extreme Drought with a portion of the west-central to southwest degraded to Exceptional Drought (D4). Although the majority of the month was abnormally warm and very dry, some relief came during the very last few days of the month where  3 to 6 of rain fell with some isolated areas seeing even more. This allowed the majority of the county to improve in drought category before going into the first week of Aug. A small sliver of the far southwest corner remained in D4 while with the south to southwest half in D3 still and the north to northeast half improving to D2 by the end of the month.

During the first half of the month the southwest two thirds of Armstrong County went from Severe Drought (D2) to Extreme Drought (D3) due to a dry start to the month. The other northeastern third went from Moderate Drought (D1) to Severe Drought (D2) at the same time. A late month rain event during the last few days led a one categorical improvement for all areas except for the far southern quarter to third of the county which remained in Extreme Drought (D3).

A small area in the far southern portion of the county was in Severe Drought (D2) at the beginning of the month. The majority of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1) with a small area in the far northern portion of the county was only abnormally dry (D0). A few isolated areas of the county received just above 2 of rain for the month, while the rest of the county only received 0.5 to 1.5 of rain.  With this still being between 1 and 2 below normal especially in the southern half of the county degradation were observed in drought conditions by the end of the month. The county ended with the far southwest corner in Extreme Drought (D3) and the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2).

Donley County started the month of July primarily in Moderate Drought (D1) with the exception of a small portion in the far southwest corner that was in Severe Drought (D2). A few rainfall events during the month led to a spread of 1.5 to 3 of rain being received over the course of the month. This is still well below normal for the month of July and led to the area of Moderate Drought degrading to Severe Drought and the area of Severe Drought degrading to Extreme Drought (D3) in the far southwest by the end of the month. The one exception was a late in the month event led to the far northwest corner switching fright back to Moderate Drought by Aug 1.

Roberts County began the month of July mostly in Moderate Drought (D1), except for the far southern and eastern sliver of the county in Abnormally Dry (D0). Overall the county was below normal for precipitation, but the north east was the only portion above normal by a few inches of rainfall. Thus Roberts County ended the month of July in mostly Severe Drought (D2) due to the below normal precipitation despite 1 to 3 of rainfall and only a small sliver in the south and east in Moderate Drought.

Much of Ochiltree County, except the far north, started the month of July with Moderate Drought (D1) conditions. However, an unfortunate month of little precipitation lead to the entire county under Severe Drought (D2) conditions through most of the month and even worsening to Extreme Drought (D3) across the northwest portion by the last week of the month. A rain event on the last three days of the month (July 29-31) lead to 1 to 3 of rainfall across the northwest portion of the county, which helped to eliminate the extreme drought and end the month of July completely in severe drought across the county.

Gray County was only abnormally dry (D0) at the beginning of the month. July was abnormally dry with Moderate Drought (D1) returning by mid week. By the third week 75% of the county slipped into Severe Drought (D2).  It wasn't till a decent rain event during the last few days of the month that helped the county end in Moderate Drought with the exception of the far southeast corner of the county. The county's overall monthly rain total ended with a large range from 1.5 to 5.

Wheeler County started the month out with only abnormally dry conditions (D0). However, July was abnormally dry and hot with drought conditions reappearing by mid month. The entire county was in Moderate Drought (D1) by mid month and by the third week all but the most northern quarter of the county slipped into Severe Drought (D2). A slight improvement in the far northwest portion of D2 improved to D1 during the last few days of the month leaving the southeast two thirds in D2 with a 0.5 to 1.5 deficit for the month. The northwest third ended the month in D1 with a 0.1 to 0.5 deficit for the month.
Quarter to half dollar size hail was reported to be covering the ground.

A small tornado developed over open country and moved northeast. The tornado lasted for less than one minute and was confirmed from spotter video. The tornado path length and path width were estimated. No damage or injuries were reported.

A small tornado developed over open country and moved northeast. The tornado lasted for less than one minute and was confirmed from spotter video. The path length and path width were estimated. No damage or injuries were reported.
Hailstones were reported to be up to baseball size along Texas State Highway 273.
A few golf ball size hailstones reported mixed in with slightly smaller stones.
The wind gust was measured at the Texas Mesonet station located one mile east of McLean.
Hailstones were reported to be completely covering the ground.
Hail was reported south of Wheeler on U.S. Highway 83.
Penny to quarter size hail was reported.
The hail was reported at rest area.
Hail was reported to be covering the ground.
Hailstones reported to be as large as baseballs broke out windows in several homes and caused damage to tractors and vehicles.
The hail was reported to be quarter size to golf ball size.
Hail was reported on County Road 19 and County Line Road.
An apparent heat burst produced strong wind gusts which were measured on the trained spotter's home weather instrument.

Outflow winds from thunderstorms downed several power lines and fifteen power poles in Hooker and west of Hooker with a report of two small grass fires ongoing. Power was lost in Hooker for about six hours. The downed power poles west of Hooker on U.S. Highway 54 and north sparked a wheat stubble fire. Then...high winds apparently blew a county equipment shed apart...opening a gas line that was ignited by a spark from metal or electricity. The county lost some pieces of equipment but most items stored in the shed were saved.
A county barn was blown over damaging a few houses and vehicles. Power lines were also reported to be blown down. No injuries were reported.
Power lines were reported to be down along U.S. Highway 412 in southeastern Texas County.

Cimarron County started the month of August with a portion of the northwestern part of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). During the month the county received 1.3 to 3.0 with locally higher amounts especially in the west.  Most of the this rain fell in the latter part of the month with some of the southeast degrading to D3 from D2.  The rain did help all areas of D3 to improve to D2 by the end of the month with the southwest portion of the county actually improving to Moderate Drought (D1).  The county remained 2 to 6 short on rain year to date.

Texas County started the month with a small strip from the south-central to the northeast in Extreme Drought (D3), while a majority of the county began in Severe Drought (D2). The month of August was abnormally dry with the county ending 0.5 to 2.0 below normal for the month, with the worst being in the western portions. The majority of the county fell into D3 with a small area to the south and southeast of Guymon that fell completely into Exceptional Drought (D4) by the month's end. The decent amount of rain the month prior managed to keep the far western portions of the county in D2.

The northern  third to half of the county started the month of August in Extreme Drought (D3), while the southern half was mostly in Severe Drought (D2) with the far southeast in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received 1 to 2 of rain during the month, which was still short of the monthly normal by 0.5 to 1.75. Only minor changes occurred in the drought with a slight expansion of D3 in the far west central portion of the county.

Dallam County started the month of August with a small sliver of the far western portion of the county in Extreme Drought (D3), with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The month was abnormally dry for August with only 0.5 to 2.0 and a few isolated areas possibly getting 3.0.  The majority of the county ended the month 1 to 2 below normal. This led to a slight expansion of D3 in the west with the rest of the county remaining in D2 at the end of the month. The county remained in a 2 to 6 deficit year to date.

Sherman County started the month of August in Severe Drought (D2). By mid month the eastern half of the county slipped into Extreme Drought (D3). The majority of the county received 0.5 to 2.0, with the monthly normal closer to 3.0. This led to most of the county remaining with no change. There was a small area in the far south central to southeast that improved from D3 back to D2. Otherwise the county ended the month with no changes since mid-month. The county remained in a 2 to 6 deficit year to date.

Hansford County started the month in Severe Drought (D2) across the entire county. About half of the county, in the northwest, fell into Extreme Drought (D3) by the end of the month. This was due to much of the county ending the month 0.5 to 2 below normal.

Ochiltree County started the month out in Severe Drought (D2), with the exception of a small area in the far southeast that was in Moderate Drought (D1). The county managed to receive enough rain to keep conditions from degrading with no changes by the end of the month. Despite only being around a 1 to 2 deficit for the month, much of the county remained in a 2 to 4 deficit over the last three months.

Around a third of the county in the west central to northwest portion of the county started the month in Severe Drought (D2), while the rest of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1). The county ended the this month plus the last two months with a 3 month deficit around 2 to 6. The area of D2 expanded to cover much of the western half of the county.

The vast majority of Hartley County started the month in Severe Drought (D2) with a very small portion of the far northwest corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). This area of D3 expanded to the southeast over the course of the month with this area only receiving 0.25 to 0.50 of rain over the course of the month. The rest of the county remained in D2 where 0.75 to upwards of 3.00 of rain fell.  Much of the county remained in a 1 to 4 deficit going back 3 months.

Moore County started the month of August entirely in Severe Drought (D2). Over the course of the month the southern portions of the county received 1.5 to 4 of rain allowing an improvement to Moderate Drought (D1), while the north only received 1.5 of rain or less keeping one third of the county in the north in D2.

Hutchinson County started the month in Severe Drought (D2). The month of August was dry compared to normal with much of the county being 0.5 to 1.5 below normal for the month. The far southern portion of the county received just enough rain over the month and in the previous month of July for conditions to improve to Moderate Drought (D1).

Roberts County started the month with a majority of the county in Severe Drought (D2) conditions with exception to the far southern and far eastern portions that began in Moderate Drought (D1) conditions. The southeast corner of the county received 0.5 to 1.5 above normal rainfall for the month, while the far western portions received 0.5 to 1.5 below normal. The rest of the county was right around normal for the month of August. About a third of the county in the northwest corner stayed in D2, while the far southern and southeastern portions of the county improved to Abnormally Dry (D0) and the rest of the county improved to Moderate Drought (D1) conditions.

Oldham County started the month with the western third to half of the county in Extreme Drought (D3), while the rest of the county to the east was in Severe Drought (D2).  The western part of the county that was in D3 received 1 to 2 above normal rainfall allowing this part of the county to improve to Moderate Drought (D1) by the end of the month. The rest of the county received around 1 below normal rainfall for the month with just enough rain to improve only one category to D1 from D2.

The southeast two thirds of Wheeler County started the month of August in Severe Drought (D2) with the northwest third in Moderate Drought (D1). Over the course of the month 2 to 5 of rain fell, improving the northwest half to two thirds of the county to abnormally dry conditions (D0) and the southeastern portions to D1.

The southwestern half of the county was in Exceptional Drought (D4) at the start of the month. The rest of the county was in Extreme Drought (D3) with a small portion of the northeast corner in Severe Drought (D2). The western portions received 2 to 5 of rain, while the eastern portions only received 1 to 2 over the course of the month. This led to an improvement in conditions with the southwest two-thirds ending the month in D2 and the northeastern third ending the month in Moderate Drought (D1). Much of the southern half of the county remained in a 6 to 12 deficit year to date.

At the start of August Randall County was in Severe Drought (D2) in the north to northeast half of the county while the south to southwest was in  either Extreme Drought (D3) or Exceptional Drought (D4). The area of D4 was the far southwest corner. Over the course of the month the eastern half of the county received 2 to 5 of rain while the western half only received 1 to 3 of rain. Conditions improved by months end with the southwest corner still in D2 while the rest of the county improved to Moderate Drought (D1) conditions. The southwest corner in D2 remained in a 6 to 12 deficit year to date.

The southern third of Armstrong County started the month in Extreme Drought (D3). The northeastern portion of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1) with much of the central to western portions of the county in Severe Drought (D2). Over the course of the month, the northern half of the county received 1.5 to 4 of rain, while the southern half received 3 to 6.  Drought conditions improved in the north to Abnormally Dry (D0), while the central portions improved to D1. The far south, even with all the rain received during the month remained in D2 with a 4 to 8 deficit year to date.

The far south to southeastern portions of the county started the month of August in Extreme Drought (D3) conditions. The rest of the county was in Severe Drought (D2). The area of D3 expanded north a bit through the month. The northwest corner of the county improved to Moderate Drought (D1) after receiving 3 to 4 over the course of the month. The rest of the county remained in D2 with only receiving 1 to 2.5 over the month. Much of the county remained in a 4 to 12 deficit year to date.

The vast majority of Donley County started August off in Severe Drought (D2) with the exception of the northwest corner which was in Moderate Drought (D1) and the very far southwest corner in Extreme Drought (D3). Over the course of the month much of the county received 2 to 6 of rain.  The northwest corner improved to Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions while the central to northeastern portions improved to D1. The far southern third of the county remained in Severe Drought (D2) with the far southwest corner improving to D2. The southern portion of the county remained in D2 with a 6 to 10 deficit year to date.

Gray County started the month of August with the far southeast corner of the county in Severe Drought (D2) while the rest of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1). Within the first week the county received enough rain for the area of D2 to improve to D1 as well as areas in D1 across central portions of the county to improve to D0 (Abnormally Dry).  With 3 to 5 of rainfall across the county by the end of the month the vast majority of the county improved to D0, with the exception of a small area in the northwest and southeast that remained in D1.

The majority of Hemphill County started the month of August with Moderate Drought (D1) and a small area in the north-central part of the county in Severe Drought (D2). By mid-week the area of D2 improved to Moderate Drought (D1). The far northern portion of the county received near normal precipitation for the month while the rest of the county received 2 to 3 above normal. This rainfall improved conditions to all but the northwest corner of the county, with mostly Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions to having no drought status by the end of the month.

Potter County started the month in Severe Drought (D2) with the exception of a small area in the far east-central portion of the county that was in Moderate Drought (D1). The majority of the county improved to D1 by mid-month with areas around Amarillo staying in D2. By the third week of the month the rest of the area of D2 improved to D1 conditions too. The county remained in a 2 to 8 deficit year to date by the end of August.

Carson County started the month of August with the far northern and far southwestern portions of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The rest of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1). Within the first week enough rain fell in the southwest and northwest corner of the county to change from D2 to D1. It was not until the third week when the rest of the northern area of D2 improved to D1. Much of the county received near normal to above normal rainfall during the month with the majority of the central to southern portions of the county improving to Abnormally Dry (D0) status. A good portion of the county, mainly central portions, ended the month with above normal rainfall year to date. The rest of the county ended the month with just slightly below normal rainfall year to date.
The roof of a well house was blown off and  hit a gazebo, causing damage. The well house  itself was blown over. Barn doors were  damaged, and a few large tree limbs were  blown down.

The landspout tornado damaged some out buildings and ripped half the roof off an older mobile home which was one of the main damage indicators for this event. Several empty semi tractor trailers at a trucking company were flipped and pushed several yards. Toward the end of the damage path, the tornado destroyed a poorly constructed and old cabin/storage building. Power lines along the path were not damaged and a mobile home directly adjacent to the poorly constructed destroyed building only showed very minor damage. These factors suggest a high end EF0 rating with maximum winds around 85 mph. This survey utilized pictures and information provided by Moore County Emergency management. The landspout was well documented on video by numerous witnesses.
Three feet of running water was observed running over Webb Rd near HWY 136 where it dips down.
Video received on social media showing water running  over a rural road from ditch to ditch.
Standing water of a couple to 6��� observed on  back roads in and around Parsley Rd and  Bertrand south of HWY 136.
Standing water seen on broadcast media  webcam covering theater parking lot in Palo Duro State Park.
Three to four inches diameter tree  branches down in Tangle Aire subdivision.
Half of a tree was down with a diameter of  approximately 12��� to 18��� at the Lake Tanglewood golf course.
Billboard boards blown off just west of  Sunday Canyon Rd and TX HWY 217.
Damage reported of downed trees on Kenneth AVE, along with a roof blown off of a shed, and a nearby baseball field dugout cover was blown  over.

The tornado developed four miles north northwest of Channing at 1429 CST and moved northeast. There were multiple reports from trained spotters...the broadcast media...and an off-duty National Weather Service employee of the tornado touching the ground. The tornado remained over open country and ended at 1435 CST roughly four to five miles north of Channing. No structural damage or injuries were reported. The tornado path length and path width were estimated. There were reports that four inch diameter tree branches were snapped off by the tornado.

This tornado formed six miles northeast of Channing in Hartley County and tracked east northeast for about five miles before exiting Hartley County about ten and a half miles east northeast of Channing at 1444 CST. The tornado continued in western Moore County for about another two miles...before dissipating at 1449 CST. The tornado remained over open country and no damage or injuries were reported. The tornado path length and path width were estimated.

This tornado formed six miles northeast of Channing in Hartley County and entered western Moore County about ten miles southwest of Dumas at 1444 CST. The tornado then continued moving east northeast for another two miles before dissipating about eight miles southwest of Dumas at 1449 CST. The tornado tracked across Middlewell Road just south of Farm to Market Road 722 at 1448 CST by law enforcement officials which was also confirmed by off-duty National Weather Service employees. No damage or injuries were reported and the tornado remained over open country. The tornado path length and path width were estimated.

This tornado developed at 1553 CST about seven miles west southwest of Pringle and moved northeast for about a half mile. The tornado then dissipated at 1554 CST and remained over open country. No damage or injuries were reported. The tornado path length and path width were estimated.
The hail was reported to be quarter size to golf ball size.
Nickel size to quarter size hail was reported on Farm to Market Road 722 just west of the Hartley and Moore County line.
Golf ball size hail was reported on Farm to Market Road 722 just southwest of Dumas.
Golf ball size hail lasted nearly thirty minutes and broke the windows on a mobile home.

Most of Cimarron County received less than 0.50 inch of rain for the entire month of September. There were some small areas in the far northeast and southeast portions of the county that received upwards of an inch of rain. What rain that did fall only kept the county from degrading further into drought by the end of the month with the vast majority of the county starting and ending the month in Severe Drought (D2). The exceptions were the southwest and a portion of the county in the far north that started and ended the month in Moderate Drought (D1).   Much of the county in D2 remained in a 4 to 8 inch deficit dating back to September of last year.

Texas County continued to be in poor shape with extreme (D3) to exceptional (D4) drought conditions through the month of September. September added another 1 to 2 inch deficit to the county. Over the past 90 days the county maintained a 2 to 6 inch deficit. Over the past year (since Sep 2021), the county continued to have a 6 to 12 inch deficit especially across the southern half of the county.

The northern half of Beaver County started the month of September in Extreme Drought (D3). While the southern half started the month in Severe Drought (D2) with the exception of the far southeast corner being in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received 0.1 to 1.0 inches of rain during the month. The only change that occurred in drought was the area of D1 in the far southeast slipped into D2 with the rest of the southern half of the county.  Much of the county remained in a 6 to 12 inch deficit dating back to September of 2021.

Overall dry conditions continued through the month of September with Dallam County only receiving 0.5 to 1 inch across the east and 0.10 to 0.50 inches across central and western portions. There was an isolated area in the far west that received 1 to 3 inches but this did not improve conditions where a year-to-date deficit of 6 to 12 inch remained. The western quarter of the county started and ended the month in extreme drought (D3) while the rest of the county started and ended the month in severe drought (D2).

Sherman County only received 0.5 to 1.0 inch of precipitation through the month of September. Overall the deficit continued to build with the county seeing a 4 to 12 inch deficit year to date. The northeastern quarter or so of the county started and ended the month of September in extreme drought (D3) while the rest of the county started and ended the month in severe drought (D2).

The northwestern half of Hansford County started the month of September in extreme drought (D3), while the rest of the county started in severe drought (D2). The majority of the county only received an inch or less of precipitation leading to an increase in the deficit. Hansford County stayed in a 4 to 12 inch deficit year to date by months end leaving the areas of D3 and D2 with no change.

The southeastern corner of Ochiltree County received 1.5 to 2.5 inches of rain during the month of September. The rest of the county received less than 1.5 inches with isolated areas only receiving 0.1 to 0.25 inches. Almost the entire county started the month in severe drought (D2) and ended the month in severe drought (D2) with the exception of a very small portion in the far southeast corner that started and ended in moderate drought (D1).

The western half of Lipscomb County started the month of September in severe drought (D2) while the east was in moderate drought (D1).  Much of the county ended the month of September 2 to 3 inches below normal. This led to conditions remaining the same except in the far northeast corner that degraded into D2 from D1.  Much of the county remained in a 4 to 8 inch deficit year to date.

The far western portion of Hartley County started the month in Extreme Drought (D3) with the rest of the northwestern half in Severe Drought (D2). The southeastern half was in Moderate Drought (D1). Much of the county ended the month around 2 inches below normal for precipitation. This led to zero improvements and ending the month in the same conditions. The county remains in a 4 to 8 inch inch precipitation deficit year to date.

Moore County started the month of September with the northern third in Severe Drought (D2) and the southern two thirds in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received 0.5 to 2 inches of rain over the course of the month. This rainfall was not enough to improve conditions, thus ending the month in the same drought categories that existed at the start of the month. Moore County remained in a 2 to 6 inch deficit year to date.

The northern two thirds of Hutchinson County started the month of September in Severe Drought (D2) with the southern third in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received anywhere between 0.10 to 1.00 inch over the course of the month. Conditions were unable to improve with the areas of D2 and D1 staying. Hutchinson County ended the month with a  4 to 8 inch rainfall deficit year to date.

A small portion of southeast Roberts County started the month in Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions with the the northwest third or so of the county in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. The central portion of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1). The southwest corner of the county received upwards of 1 inch of rain while the northeast half only received upwards of 0.5 inches max. With the county ending the month of September below normal, conditions stayed unchanged by the 27th. The county remained in a 4 to 8 inch deficit year to date.

The southwest half to two thirds of the county started the month of September in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. Deaf Smith County received 0 to 1 inches of rainfall over the course of the month. Relying on previous months rainfall, conditions remained unchanged through the end of the month. The county remained in a  4 to 12 inch rainfall deficit year to date.

Randall County started the month of September with the far southwest corner in Severe Drought (D2) and the rest of the county in Moderate Drought (D1). The county only received around 0.10 to 0.50 inches in the area of D1, and the area of D2 received 0.50 to 1.00 inch of rain. This rain amount left the county below normal for the month, leaving the classifications of drought the same. The county remained in a  4 to 12 inch deficit in rainfall year to date.

Collingsworth County started the month of September with the far southeast corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) and the northwest corner in Moderate Drought (D1) with the majority of area in the central part of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The majority of the county received 1 to 1.5 inch of rainfall while the far southeast corner only received 0.1 to 0.25 inches of rainfall. Categories of drought remained unchanged by months end. Much of Collingsworth County remained in a 6 to 12 inch rainfall deficit year to date.

The northern portion of Armstrong County started the month in Abnormally Dry (D0) conditions, while the far southern portion was in Severe Drought (D2). The central portion was in Moderate Drought (D1). Some early rainfall in addition to rainfall on the very last day of August led to conditions improving to D1 by September 6th. Armstrong County ended the month with a 4 to 8 inch rainfall deficit year to date.

Collingsworth County started the month of September with the far southeast corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) and the northwest corner in Moderate Drought (D1) with the majority of area in the central part of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The majority of the county received 1 to 1.5 inches of rainfall while the far southeast corner only received 0.1 to 0.25 inches of rainfall. Categories of drought remained unchanged by months end. Much of Collingsworth County remains in a 6 to 12 inch rainfall deficit year to date.

The broadcast media reported that the field house at River Road High School had part of its roof blown off.
A trained spotter reported small limbs broken off a tree at Interstate 40 and Eastern Street.

Much of Cimarron County started the month of October in Severe Drought (D2) with the exception of a portion in the southwest and far north that were in Moderate Drought (D1). Within the first week of the month the area of D1 in the southwest shrank with D2 expanding. In the east drought conditions worsened with Extreme Drought (D3) expanding from Texas County into eastern portions of Cimarron County. Cimarron County received half an inch to an inch below normal rainfall for the month.  By mid month the far northern area of D1 conditions degraded to D2. Much of the county remains in a 4 to 10 deficit year to date.

Much of the county started the month off in Extreme Drought (D3) to Exceptional Drought (D4) with a small portion of the far west and southeastern corner of the county were in Severe Drought (D2). Over the course of the month conditions continued to degrade with half of the county ended the month in D4 and the other half in D3. The area of D4 remained across central portions of the county surrounded by D3 in the west and east. The county ended the month 1 to 2.5 below normal for October Rainfall. The county remains in an 8 to 12 deficit year to date.

Beaver County started the month off with the northern one half to two thirds of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). The remaining southern portion of the county started the month off in Severe Drought (D2). Over the course of the month conditions worsened with the area of D2 degrading to D3 and the northeast corner degrading to Exceptional Drought (D4). The county  ended the month of October 1 to 2 below normal in rainfall. The county also remains in an 8 to 12 deficit year to date.

The far western quarter to third of the county started the month of October in Extreme Drought (D3) conditions. The rest of the county started the month off with Severe Drought (D2) conditions. With in the first week D3 conditions spread across much of the county with the far western portion developing Exceptional Drought (D4) conditions and stayed with these drought conditions through the end of the month with no improvements.  The county ended the month of October 0.5 to 1.5 below normal for the month. Also, the county remained in a 4 to 8 deficit year to date.

Sherman County started the month with Severe Drought (D2) conditions in the southwestern two thirds. The northeastern third was in Extreme Drought (D3). Within the first couple of days of month the area of D3 in the northeast degraded into Exceptional Drought (D4) conditions and all but the southwest corner of D2 degraded into D3 conditions. With the exception of the southwest corner that ended the month with near normal rainfall, the rest of the county ended the month of October 0.5 to 1.5 below normal for the month. The majority of the county remained in a 6 to 10 deficit year to date.

The northwest half to two thirds of Hansford County started the month of October in Extreme Drought (D3) conditions with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. Within the first few days the area of D3 degraded to Exceptional Drought (D4) will the area of D2 degraded to D3. With much of the county receiving below normal rainfall for the month these drought conditions stayed through the entire month. The county remained in a 6 to 10 deficit year to date.

Ochiltree County started the month of October in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. Within the first few days the western half and northwest corner degraded into Extreme Drought (D3) conditions. With much of the county receiving 0.5 to 1.5 below normal rainfall for Oct, the county stayed with these drought classifications through the end of the month. Ochiltree County remained in a 4 to 8 deficit year to date.

Lipscomb County started the month of October in Severe Drought (D2) in the northwest half of the county. The southwest half was in Moderate Drought (D1). Conditions quickly degraded through the month with the county ending the month with Extreme Drought (D3) conditions across the northern half of the county and D2 across the southern half of the month. Much of Lipscomb County saw another 0.5 to 1.5 added to the rainfall deficit. The county had a 6 to 10 deficit year to date at the end of October.

A small portion of of the far northwestern county started the month of October in Extreme Drought (D3) conditions with Severe Drought (D2) conditions across the remaining western and northern portion of the county. The southeast third to half of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1) at the beginning of the month. Conditions degraded through the month with the area of D1 falling into D2 and the area of D3 expanding ever so slightly over the northwest corner of the county. Much of the county had a normal rainfall for the month but this was not enough to improve or maintain the conditions at the beginning of the month. The county remained in a 4 to 8 rainfall deficit year to date.

Moore County started out the month with Severe Drought (D2) conditions across the northern third of the county. The southern two thirds were in Moderate Drought (D1). Conditions gradually degraded over the month despite  near normal rainfall for the month. The county ended the month with the northeastern corner in Extreme Drought (D3) and all of the area in D1 degrading to D2. The county remained in a 4 to 8 rainfall deficit year to date.

Hutchinson County started the month with Severe Drought (D2) conditions across the northern half to two thirds of the county. The southern portion of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1). Despite some areas of the county receiving around an inch of rain above normal for the month and the majority of the county receiving near normal rainfall drought conditions worsened over the area. A long lasting deficit contributed to the north to northeastern half or so of the county developed Extreme Drought (D3) and the expansion of D2 across the rest of the southern half of the county.  Much of the county remained in a 4 to 8 deficit year to date at the end of October.

Roberts County started the month of October with Severe Drought (D2) conditions across the northwestern third of the county. By months end Extreme Drought (D3) encompassed the northwest while all but the southeast corner slipped into D2 conditions. Despite near normal rainfall being received for the month, Roberts County remained in a 4 to 8 deficit year to date.

Deaf Smith County started the month of October with the southwest two thirds of the county in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. Within the first few days the remaining area of Moderate Drought (D1) degraded into D2 conditions with the far southern portion of the county degrading into Extreme Drought (D3).  The northwest portion of the county did receive 1 to 2 of above normal rainfall by mid month with this area improving to D1. Much of the county remained in a 4 to 8 rainfall deficit year to date.

Randall County started the month of October with the southwest corner in Severe Drought (D2) and the rest of the county in Moderate Drought (D1). Within the first few days a small portion of the far southwest corner degraded into Extreme Drought (D3) conditions while the rest of the western half of the county degraded into D2 drought. The county ended the month with the western half in at least D2 conditions an a rainfall deficit of 4 to 8 year to date.

Collingsworth County started the month of October with the southeast two thirds of the county in Severe Drought (D2) to Extreme Drought (D3) conditions. This portion of the county did received near normal to below normal rainfall for the month which kept conditions relatively the same through the end of the month. The county remained in a 6 to 10 rainfall deficit year to date.

Hemphill County started the month of October with Abnormally Dry (D0) to Moderate Drought (D1) conditions. Within the first few days of the month conditions were reclassified in the north and far southeast to Severe Drought (D2) and stayed this way through the end of the month.  Much of the northeastern half of the county ended the month of October around an inch below normal while the southwest third to half end the month near normal for precipitation. The county remained in a 2 to 6 deficit year to date.

Oldham County started the month of October in Moderate Drought (D1). Continuing dryness had the entire county reclassified in Severe Drought (D2) within the first few days. A change in weather pattern brought some much needed rain to the southwest corner of the county into Deaf Smith County and portions of eastern New Mexico. The southwest corner ended up with 2 to 3 of rain during mid month. This allowed an improvement for southwest portions and a reclassification back into D1. The county continued a deficit of about 2 to 6 deficit year to date for areas in D2 at the end of the month.

Potter County started the month of October classified in Moderate Drought (D1).  A continuing dry spell had the entire county reclassified in Severe Drought (D2) within the first few days of the month. Multiple rounds of rain during the month added up to around 2 to 3 of rain being received in the southeast corner of the county. This brough some improvement and a reclassification into D1 by the end of the month. The county continued a 4 to 8 deficit year to date.

Carson County started the month of Oct with Moderate Drought (D1) conditions. Much of the southern portions of the county received upwards of 4 of rain over the month allowing the south to remain in D1. The north to northwestern half received closer to 2 during the month and saw conditions degrade with a reclassification into Severe Drought (D2) starting in the first few days and lasting through the end of the month.  A few localized areas have a rainfall surplus for the year while the rest of the county remained with a 2 to 6 deficit year to date.

Carson County started the month of Oct with Moderate Drought (D1) conditions. A continuing dry spell had the northwest corner of the county reclassified into Severe Drought (D2) within the first days. With only 1 to 2 of rain being received in northwest corner the D2 classification stayed through the end of the month. The rest of the county received 2 to 4 of rain and kept the classification of moderate drought.

This tornado track was estimated based on photos and eyewitness accounts. The tornado was moved northeast and was on the ground for just under 2 minutes. No damage was found, however the tornado didn't encounter any damage indicators along the path as|it remained in open grasslands. Given the lack of damage indicators, an unknown rating has been assigned.

This tornado was documented by multiple storm chasers with photos and video as it crossed US Highway 270 south of Beaver, Oklahoma. The tornado was on the ground for approximately one minute. With no damage reported to the power lines that the tornado crossed along the highway and no other damage indicators along the path which remained in open grassland areas, the tornado was rated an EF0.|The track and width were estimated based on eye witness reports, radar signatures and photographs. The maximum estimated wind speeds were 80 mph.

Cimarron County started the month of January with the eastern third of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) while the rest of the county was in Severe Drought (D2). One tiny exception was a very small area in the far east central portion of the county that was still in Moderate Drought (D1). The county continued to be dry with the month of January ending with near normal to slightly below normal rainfall. Conditions did worsen slightly with the far northeastern corner of the county slipping into Exceptional Drought (D4) and the expansion of D3 into central portions of the county. The area of D1 degraded to D2 as well. The county remained in a 2 to 4 rainfall deficit since October first of last year.

Texas County started and ended the month with the vast majority of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4), with the rest of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). There was only a slight expansion of D4 in the far west central part of the county. The county ended the month with near normal to slightly below normal precipitation. The county also continued a 2 to 4 rainfall deficit since October first.

Beaver County started and ended the month of January with the vast majority of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) conditions. The exception being the far northeastern corner of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4).  The county received 0.25 to 0.5 of precipitation for the month. With a large rain deficit dating back a year, and a 2 to 6 deficit dating back to October First, drought conditions are far from improving.

Dallam County started the month of January with western portions of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4), central to northeastern portions in Extreme Drought (D3), and a portion of the north central and southeastern county in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. A large portion of the county only received less than an quarter to less than a tenth of an inch of precipitation.  County remains in a 2 to 4 deficit dating back to 10/1/2022.

Sherman County started and ended the month with the northeast third of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4), with Extreme Drought (D3) through the central portions, and a small area in the southwest corner in Severe Drought (D2). The county received 0.40 or less of precipitation for the month of Jan. The county remained in a 2 to 4 deficit dating back to 10/1/2022.

The northwest third to half of Hansford County started and ended the month of Jan in Exceptional Drought (D4) conditions. The rest of the county remained in Extreme Drought (D3) conditions through the month. A good portion of the county received 0.25 to 0.50 during the month. Drought conditions remained unchanged as a 2 to 4 deficit dating back 10/1/2022 continued.

The central to southeastern corner of the county started and ended the month in Severe Drought (D2).  During the month the county received less than 0.25 up to just under 0.50  of precipitation. A 2 to 4 deficit dating back to 10/1/2022 continued.

Lipscomb County started and ended the month with the northern half of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) with the southern half in Severe Drought (D2). The county received between 0.25 and 0.50 of precipitation over the course of the month. However, a 2 to 4 deficit since October 1st continued.

Hartley County started and ended the month of January with the northwest corner in Extreme Drought (D3) and the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The eastern half of the county received around 0.25 to 0.5 of precipitation while the western half received less than 0.25 of precipitation.  The county still continued a 1 to 2 deficit dating back to October.

Moore County started and ended the month of Jan with the far northeast corner of the county in Extreme Drought with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). Much of the county received less than 0.25 of precipitation through the month. At this point the deficit continued from last year.

Hutchinson County started and ended the month with the northeastern third to half of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) and the rest of the southwest in Severe Drought (D2). The county received less than half an inch in precipitation for the month and a 6 to 12 deficit continued from last year.

Roberts County started and ended the month of Jan with the northwest corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3), central portions in Severe Drought (D2), and the far southeast corner in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received just under an inch to just under half inch of precipitation over the course of the month. Drought conditions continued as a 4 to 8 rainfall deficit continued from last year.

Hemphill County started and ended the month with the far northern portion, and the far southeastern corner in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. The county received around 0.25 to 0.50 of precipitation during the month. Drought conditions remained as there was still a continuation of  a 2 to 8 rainfall deficit from last year.

Oldham County started and ended the month of Jan with portions of the northern and eastern part of the county in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. The rest of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1). Potter County started and end the month of Jan with all but the southeast corner in Severe Drought (D2).  The southeast was in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received anywhere from 0.25 to just under an inch of precipitation over the course of the month. Drought conditions remained unchanged as a yearly deficit of 4 to 10 from last year continued.

Carson County started and ended the month of Jan with the north to northwest in Severe Drought (D2) conditions while the southern portions were in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received anywhere from 0.25 to just under an inch of precipitation over the course of the month. Drought conditions remained unchanged as a yearly deficit of 4 to 10 from last year continued.

Gray County started and ended the month of Jan with the northwest portion in Severe Drought (D2) while the rest of the county was in Moderate Drought (D1). The county received 0.25 to 0.5 of precipitation over the course of the month. Drought conditions remained unchanged as a yearly deficit of 2 to 6 from last year continued.

Beaver County started the month of February with the northeast corner of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4) with the rest of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). There was a wide range of total precipitation through the month with some small areas receiving as little as 0.01 with some small areas receiving just below and inch of liquid. The majority of the area received less than 0.25 of precipitation. Overall deficits continued with not much changing in drought status other than the far northern portion of the county slipping into D4.

The vast majority of Texas County started the month of Feb in Exceptional Drought (D4). The exception being the southeastern quarter of the county and a tiny area in the southwestern corner that were in Extreme Drought (D3). Within the first week the southwest corner joined the rest of the county in D4. By the end of the month the southeastern area of D3 shrunk dramatically as D4 continued to over take remaining areas of the county. Most of the county received less than 0.25 of liquid precipitation during the month. The county continued to remain in a prolong dry period with a large part of the southern portion received less than 10 of rain last year, with the rest of the county receiving less than 15 last year. The majority of the county had received less than half an inch of moisture over Jan and Feb prolonging a 8 to 12 deficit over the last 365 days.

Cimarron County started the month of Feb with the western half of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The eastern half was in Extreme Drought (D3) with a small portion of the northeast corner in Exceptional Drought (D4). With the county receiving less than half an inch of moisture the county continued to remain parched. The area of D2 shrunk, with only a portion of the southwest remaining in D2 as D3 continued to expand. D4 conditions expanded to encompass almost the whole eastern half of the county by months end as well. The area of D2 remained in a 2 to 6 deficit since last Feb, while the rest of the county remained in a 6 to 12 deficit dating back to Feb of last year.

The northern and wester portions of the county remained in a 6 to 12 rainfall deficit dating back to Feb of last year as the county received less than half an inch to less than a quarter of an inch of precipitation this Feb. This left the western quarter to a third of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4) with the majority of the county remaining in Extreme Drought (D4). There was a  small portion of the southeast that remained in Severe Drought (D2).

Sherman County started the month of Feb with Severe Drought (D2) to the southwest, Extreme Drought (D3) across central portions, and Exceptional Drought (D4) in the northeastern portion of the county. With Feb being a climatological dry month precipitation received even if it was slightly below to near normal the county remained in a prolong deficit. The area of D4 had expanded westward slightly for the month of Feb. The county remained in a 6 to 12 deficit dating back to Feb of last year.

Hansford County was in Exceptional Drought (D4) to the northwest and Extreme Drought (D3) to the southeast during the month of Feb. Much of the county received upwards of 0.5 to 1 of precipitation during the month. There was a small area in the northeast that had received less than half an inch and this area went from D3 to D4 by months end. The county remained in an 8 to 12 rainfall deficit since Feb of 2022.

Ochiltree County started the month with the northern and western portions of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) and the central to southeastern portion in Severe Drought (D2). With February being a climatologically dry month little to no relief came during the month of February. In fact, much of the area of D2 fell into D3 by the end of the month. The county remained in a 4 to 6 deficit over the last 180 days.

Lipscomb County started the month with the northern third to half of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). The southern portion of the county was in Severe Drought (D2). With February being a climatologically dry month little to no relief came during the month of February. In fact, much of the area of D2 fell into D3 by the end of the month.  Much of the county remained in a 4 to 6 deficit over the last 180 days.

Hartley County started and ended the month of Feb with the northwest corner in Extreme Drought (D3) and the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). With February being a climatologically dry month little to no relief came during the month of February.  The county remained with a 2 to 4 deficit dating back 180 days.

Moore County started and ended the month of Feb with the far northeast corner of the county in Extreme Drought with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The county remained in a 2 to 4 rainfall deficit going back 180 days, a 4 to 10 deficit dating back 365 days.

Hutchinson County started and ended the month with the northeastern third to half of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) and the rest of the southwest in Severe Drought (D2). No Changes were made to the Oldham County drought from the end of February through the month of March: southwest Oldham County remained in D1 while the northwest, north, and east remained in D2. Most of the County received 0.25 to 0.5 of rain in March with the extreme west and extreme south received 0.50 to 1, and the northeast received 0.10 to 0.25. Relative to climatology, this comes to 25% to 50%/0.5 to 1 below normal for most of the county. The northeast received only 10% to 25%/0.5 to 1 below normal.

No changes were made to the Deaf Smith County drought from the end of February through the month of March: The northwest portion of Deaf Smith County remained in D1, the extreme southern portion of the county remained in D3, while the rest remained in D2. Southern Deaf Smith County received 0.1 to 0.25 of rain, the north-central portion of the County received 0.5 to 1 of rain, while the rest of the county received 0.25 to 0.5 of rain. This amounts to 10-25% of average/1 to 2 below average in the south and 25-50% of average/0.5 to 1 below average elsewhere.

Most of Potter County remained in D2 throughout March, but D3 was introduced in the far northeast with the March 28 update. Most of Potter County received 0.25 to 0.5, though a few localized areas along the Canadian River Valley received 0.10 to 0.25. This amounts to 25-50% of average/0.5 to 1 below average for Potter County except for the Canadian River Valley which is 10-25% of average/1 to 2 below average.

March started with eastern Randall County in D1, the extreme southwest in D3, and the rest of the County in D2. The area of D1 was replaced by D2 with the March 21 update. No changes otherwise. Most of the County received 0.25 to 0.5 of rain, but a hole of 0.1 to 0.25 was observed around Canyon. This was 10-25% of average for Canyon, eastern Randall County, and southern Randall County which is 1 to 2 of average in the east and southwest. Elsewhere in the County, it was 25-50% of average which is 0.5 to 1 below average.

Dallam County started the month of March with a small portions in the southeast in Severe Drought (D2), the far western portion of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4), and the rest of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). The county received 0.01 to less than 0.5 of precipitation for the month. Or 5% to 50% of the March monthly normal. This led to the area of D2 degrading to D3, and some portions of the already D3 into D4.

Hartley County started the month of March with the northwest corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3), of which, a very small portion in the far northwest of that was in Exceptional Drought (D4). The rest of the county was in Severe Drought (D2). The county received around 0.25 up to just under an inch of precipitation during the month. Or 10% to 50% of the March monthly normal. This led to the expansion of D4 to encompass almost the entire northwestern half of the county.

Sherman County started the month of March with the far southwest corner of the county in Severe Drought (D2), central portions of the county in Extreme Drought (D3), and the northeastern third or so of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4). The county received 0.05 to 0.50 of precipitation during the month. Or 5% to 50% of March's monthly normal. This led to much of the county slipping into D4 with the far southeast corner that was in D2 fell into the D3 category.

Moore County started the month of March with mostly Severe Drought (D2) conditions with the far northeastern corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). The county received less than 0.25 of precipitation, or 5% to 25% of March's monthly normal. This led to a big expansion of D3 across the northeastern half to two thirds of the county. Even an area of Exceptional Drought (D4) moved into the far northeastern corner of the county.

The western third of the county started the month of April in Exceptional Drought (D4), as well as a small portion of the northeastern part of the county. A small part of the southeast was in Severe Drought (D2), with the rest of the county started the month with Extreme Drought (D3). Within the first few days the area of D2 degraded to D3, as time continued with no beneficial rainfall. The areas in D4 remained the same at the end of the month and the rest of the county was in D3 at months end despite 1 to 1.5 of rainfall by late in the month.

The northwestern corner of the county started April with Extreme Drought (D3) conditions with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). Within the first couple of days in April the area of D3 expanded across the north to the northeastern corner of the county.  With much of the southern portion of the county receiving around half an inch or less of rainfall the rest of the county had degraded into  D3. A portion of the northwest fell into Exceptional Drought (D4) as well.

The southeastern corner of the county started the month in Extreme Drought (D3) while the majority of the county was in Exceptional Drought (D4). With minimal rainfall, less than 1.5 for the whole month, no changes were made to the drought categories in the county at the end of April.

Moore County started the month of April with the southwestern third to half of the county in Severe Drought (D2). The rest of the county was in Extreme Drought (D3) with a small portion in the far northeast corner in Exceptional Drought (D4). With the southwestern portion of the county in D2 receiving less than an inch in the entire month, this area degraded into Extreme Drought (D3) by the end of the month.

Hansford County started and ended the month of April with the vast majority of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4). The exception being the far southeast corner that started and ended the month in Extreme Drought (D3). Spring rains were short with only 1 to 1.5 of rainfall occurring during the month.

Ochiltree County started the month with three quarters of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4). With the exception of a small area in the southeast corner being in Severe Drought (D2), the rest of the county was classified in Extreme Drought (D3).

Lipscomb County started the month with the northwest third of the county in Exceptional Drought (D4), with the rest of the county in Extreme Drought (D3). A good portion of the the northern half to two thirds of the county received close to 2 of rain for the month. This allowed the northwestern portion of the county to improve to D3, with the entire county ending the month in D3.

Hutchinson County started the month of April with Exceptional Drought (D4) across northern portions of the county and Extreme Drought (D3) elsewhere. With the county receiving near normal to just below normal precipitation in the latter part of the month. The drought classifications for the county remained in place at the end of the month.

Roberts County started the month of April with the northwestern third of the county in Extreme Drought (D3), while the southeasthern two thirds saw Severe Drought (D2) conditions. By mid month, the continuation of dry and warm conditions plunged the entire county into D3 where the whole of the county ended the month. The county only received 50% to 90% of the monthly April normal rainfall.

Hemphill had a small area of Extreme Drought (D3) in the far northeastern corner of the county at the beginning of April. The rest of the county started the month in Severe Drought (D2).  Much of the county received 1.5 of rain or less during the month. This was below the normal April rainfall of 2 to 3. Therefore, the entire county ended the month in Extreme Drought with the exception of the far southern edge of the county that remained in D2.

Severe Drought (D2) conditions existed across the north and eastern portion of the county at the start of the month, with Moderate Drought (D1) across the remaining portions. The lack of rain continued until the entire county was in D2 by week 3 and all of the county slipping into Extreme Drought (D3) by months end.  The county had only received 0.25 to less than an inch of rainfall for the month which was only about 50% to 75% of the April normal.

The southern portion of the county started the month in Extreme Drought (D3). The northwest corner of the county started in Moderate Drought (D1) with the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). By the third week the area of D1 slipped into the D2 category and by the end of the month almost all of the county was in D3. The exception being a small area in the far eastern portion of the county that remained in D2.  The central and western portions of the county received less than 0.5 of rainfall during the month. The area that stayed D2 did receive the normal monthly April rainfall while the rest of the county was below normal.

Potter County started the month of April with the far northeastern corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3), and the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). With the county ending the month of April 0.5 to 1 below the monthly normal rainfall, the vast majority of the county ended the month in D3.

A small area of the county in the southwest corner started the month of April with Extreme Drought (D3) conditions. The rest of the county started the month in Severe Drought (D2). Extreme drought conditions overtook the northern into central portions of the county at the end of the month as these areas continued with a dry streak and only receiving  around 50% of normal April rainfall.

Carson County started the month with Extreme Drought (D3) in the north and Severe Drought (D2) elsewhere. Much of the county received 50% to 90% of the normal April rainfall. This lead to much of the county remaining unchanged in drought category with a slight increase in D3 in the far western portion of the county.

Gray County started the month in Severe Drought (D2). Much of the county received near normal April rainfall with the exception of the northwest corner. Because of this, the northwest slipped into Extreme Drought (D3).
Wheeler County started and ended the month in Severe Drought (D2). With the county only receiving 75% to 90% of the normal April rainfall during the month drought classification remained unchanged.

Armstrong County started and ended the month in Severe Drought (D2) conditions. Despite receiving near normal April rainfall over much of the county, this was not enough to offset the overall deficit for any improvements to made to the drought category.

Donley County started the month in Severe Drought (D2). The only change was a small isolated area in the southeast corner that ended the month in Extreme Drought (D3). The vast majority of the county ended the month with near normal rainfall for April.

Collingsworth County started the month with the southeast corner of the county in Extreme Drought (D3) and the rest of the county in Severe Drought (D2). By the end of the month the whole southeastern half of the county was in D3, with a small area in the far southeast corner degrading to Exceptional Drought (D4). The southeast where the degradations occurred only received 50% or less of normal April rainfall totals.

Much of Cimarron County started the month of the April in Exceptional Drought (D4). There was a portion of the southeastern part of the county that was in Extreme Drought (D3). Most of the county received 50 to 75% of the normal April rainfall. A lot of the localized areas that received near or above normal rainfall were in the area of D3. Therefore, no changes were made to the Drought Monitor during this time and the county remained in a large rainfall deficit.

Texas County started and ended the month entirely in Exceptional Drought (D4). With the exception of some isolated areas the county only received around 50% to just under 90% of normal rainfall for the month of April. Texas County continued being one of the hardest hit areas for drought in the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles.

Beaver County started the month of April with all but a small area in the southeast corner in Exceptional Drought (D4). There was at least one category improvement in the south central to southeastern portion of the county to Extreme Drought (D3). This was because some storms helped reach 100% to just over 100% of normal rainfall in the last week of April.
